approachQuestion.prompt:
Duplicate a Cross-Referenced Chain

A finite acyclic chain has n nodes, each with integer value, next and note. note is null or references any node in this chain, including itself. Return a deep-copy head: new nodes with the same values, next order and corresponding note relationships, with no references to originals. Temporary next changes are allowed but restore all original next and note links before returning. Allocation succeeds. Only head is supplied; 0 <= n <= 200000.

Input: A(3) -> B(8) -> null, A.note=B, B.note=B. Output: new A2(3) -> B2(8) -> null, A2.note=B2, B2.note=B2; originals unchanged. Empty input returns null.

Choose a method that satisfies the full contract with the best worst-case running time, breaking time ties by least auxiliary storage.

options.text: Interleave copies, separate the chains, and only then translate note using original.note.next.
options.feedback: After separation that next is an original successor, not a copy. A one-node self-note becomes null.

options.text: Insert each new copy immediately after its original. Set each copy.note to original.note.next or null. Separate the chains, restoring original next links and connecting copies to one another.
options.feedback: During interleaving, an original's next identifies its copy, translating self, forward and backward note references.

options.text: Create the result chain in order. For every original note, scan the original chain to find its position, then scan the copy chain to assign the copied target.
options.feedback: This produces a deep copy but repeatedly searches positions that interleaving resolves directly.

options.text: Copy values and next links, assigning copy.note directly to original.note.
options.feedback: If A.note=B, the copy points to original B and fails the deep-copy requirement.

Weaving each copy after its original creates an implicit original-to-copy map via next. Cross references can then use target.next. Separating the chains must restore originals as well as connect every copied next link.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (acm-b15-07-target), regardless of your Q1 choice. Here n. Choose the tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Count each node allocation, link access, identity/value comparison and machine-word operation as constant work. Include all temporary collections and call frames; exclude supplied nodes and the final returned output only. Copying or allocating k records costs k operations. No hash-table, amortized-operation or tail-call assumptions are used.

options.explanation: This pair does not describe the fixed method. Three passes process each original and copy a fixed number of times. Allocating n output nodes alone requires linear time. Those new nodes form the returned output and are excluded from auxiliary storage. Only fixed traversal references remain, without recursion or collections.
